# Feature Requirements: Slugify String Utility

## Overview

This feature provides a string utility function that converts arbitrary text into URL-friendly slugs by normalizing whitespace, removing special characters, and applying consistent formatting rules.

## Business Context

URL slugs are a fundamental requirement for web applications, content management systems, and APIs. A reliable slugify utility ensures consistent, predictable URL generation across the application, improving SEO, user experience, and system interoperability.

## Requirements

### REQ-001: Text Normalization [MUST HAVE]

**User Type**: Developer

**Description**: The slugify function must convert input text to lowercase.

**Rationale**: Lowercase normalization ensures URL consistency and prevents duplicate content issues where "Hello-World" and "hello-world" would be treated as different resources.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- All uppercase letters (A-Z) are converted to lowercase (a-z)
- Mixed-case input produces consistent lowercase output
- Non-ASCII uppercase characters are handled according to locale-independent rules

**Examples**:
- "HELLO" → "hello"
- "MixedCase" → "mixedcase"

---

### REQ-002: Whitespace and Underscore Replacement [MUST HAVE]

**User Type**: Developer

**Description**: The slugify function must replace spaces and underscores with single hyphens.

**Rationale**: Hyphens are the web standard for word separation in URLs (as opposed to underscores or spaces), improving readability and SEO compatibility.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- All space characters (U+0020) are replaced with a single hyphen (-)
- All underscore characters (_) are replaced with a single hyphen (-)
- Multiple consecutive spaces/underscores are collapsed into a single hyphen
- Replacement happens before character filtering

**Examples**:
- "hello world" → "hello-world"
- "foo_bar" → "foo-bar"
- "foo   bar" → "foo-bar"
- "foo___bar" → "foo-bar"

---

### REQ-003: Character Filtering [MUST HAVE]

**User Type**: Developer

**Description**: The slugify function must remove all characters except letters, numbers, and hyphens.

**Rationale**: Special characters and punctuation can cause encoding issues in URLs, break routing systems, or create security vulnerabilities. Restricting to alphanumeric and hyphen characters ensures maximum compatibility.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Letters (a-z) are preserved
- Numbers (0-9) are preserved
- Hyphens (-) are preserved
- All other characters (punctuation, symbols, special characters) are removed
- Character filtering applies after whitespace/underscore replacement

**Examples**:
- "hello, world!" → "hello-world"
- "foo@bar.com" → "foobarcom"
- "test#123" → "test123"

---

### REQ-004: Hyphen Normalization [MUST HAVE]

**User Type**: Developer

**Description**: The slugify function must collapse consecutive hyphens into a single hyphen.

**Rationale**: Multiple consecutive hyphens reduce URL readability and may indicate processing errors. Normalizing to single hyphens ensures clean, professional-looking URLs.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Two or more consecutive hyphens are replaced with a single hyphen
- Normalization happens after character filtering
- Single hyphens are preserved unchanged

**Examples**:
- "a--b" → "a-b"
- "a---b" → "a-b"
- "a----b" → "a-b"

---

### REQ-005: Hyphen Trimming [MUST HAVE]

**User Type**: Developer

**Description**: The slugify function must remove leading and trailing hyphens from the result.

**Rationale**: Leading or trailing hyphens appear unprofessional and may cause routing issues in some web frameworks. Clean trimming ensures slugs are ready for immediate use in URLs.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Any hyphens at the start of the string are removed
- Any hyphens at the end of the string are removed
- Trimming happens as the final step after all other transformations
- Internal hyphens are not affected

**Examples**:
- "-hello-" → "hello"
- "--foo--" → "foo"
- "-a-b-" → "a-b"

---

### REQ-006: Empty String Handling [SHOULD HAVE]

**User Type**: Developer

**Description**: The slugify function should handle edge cases where input contains only special characters or whitespace.

**Rationale**: Defensive programming prevents runtime errors and provides predictable behavior for all inputs.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Input consisting only of special characters produces an empty string
- Input consisting only of whitespace produces an empty string
- Empty string input produces empty string output

**Examples**:
- "!!!" → ""
- "   " → ""
- "" → ""

---

## User Stories

### STORY-001: URL Slug Generation

**As a** developer building a content management system
**I want** to convert article titles into URL-friendly slugs
**So that** I can generate clean, readable URLs for content pages

**Acceptance Criteria**:

```gherkin
GIVEN an article title "Hello, World! A Beginner's Guide"
WHEN I call slugify(title)
THEN I receive "hello-world-a-beginners-guide"

GIVEN a product name "Super-Fast USB_3.0 Drive!!!"
WHEN I call slugify(name)
THEN I receive "super-fast-usb-30-drive"

GIVEN user input with leading/trailing whitespace " Foo Bar "
WHEN I call slugify(input)
THEN I receive "foo-bar"
```

---

### STORY-002: Consistent URL Normalization

**As a** developer maintaining a web application
**I want** slugify to produce consistent output for similar inputs
**So that** I avoid duplicate routes and maintain URL integrity

**Acceptance Criteria**:

```gherkin
GIVEN inputs "Foo Bar", "foo_bar", and "FOO__BAR"
WHEN I call slugify on each

# Design: Slugify String Utility

**Feature ID**: slugify-string-utility
**Version**: 1.0.0
**Status**: Draft
**Created**: 2026-07-16

## Summary

The slugify utility is a pure TypeScript function added to the existing `src/utils.ts` module. It transforms arbitrary input text into URL-friendly slugs through a sequential pipeline of: lowercase normalization, whitespace/underscore replacement with hyphens, non-alphanumeric character removal, consecutive hyphen collapse, and leading/trailing hyphen trimming. This approach uses standard JavaScript string methods and regular expressions, requiring no external dependencies and matching the project's established pure-function pattern.

    45→

     9→# Feature Requirements: Slugify String Utility
    10→
    11→## Overview
    12→
    13→This feature provides a string utility function that converts arbitrary text into URL-friendly slugs by normalizing whitespace, removing special characters, and applying consistent formatting rules.
    14→
    15→## Business Context
    16→
    17→URL slugs are a fundamental requirement for web applications, content management systems, and APIs. A reliable slugify utility ensures consistent, predictable URL generation across the application, improving SEO, user experience, and system interoperability.
    18→
    19→## Requirements
    20→
    21→### REQ-001: Text Normalization [MUST HAVE]
    22→
    23→**User Type**: Developer
    24→
    25→**Description**: The slugify function must convert input text to lowercase.
    26→
    27→**Rationale**: Lowercase normalization ensures URL consistency and prevents duplicate content issues where "Hello-World" and "hello-world" would be treated as different resources.
    28→
    29→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    30→- All uppercase letters (A-Z) are converted to lowercase (a-z)
    31→- Mixed-case input produces consistent lowercase output
    32→- Non-ASCII uppercase characters are handled according to locale-independent rules
    33→
    34→**Examples**:
    35→- "HELLO" → "hello"
    36→- "MixedCase" → "mixedcase"
    37→
    38→---
    39→
    40→### REQ-002: Whitespace and Underscore Replacement [MUST HAVE]
    41→
    42→**User Type**: Developer
    43→
    44→**Description**: The slugify function must replace spaces and underscores with single hyphens.
    45→
    46→**Rationale**: Hyphens are the web standard for word separation in URLs (as opposed to underscores or spaces), improving readability and SEO compatibility.
    47→
    48→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    49→- All space characters (U+0020) are replaced with a single hyphen (-)
    50→- All underscore characters (_) are replaced with a single hyphen (-)
    51→- Multiple consecutive spaces/underscores are collapsed into a single hyphen
    52→- Replacement happens before character filtering
    53→
    54→**Examples**:
    55→- "hello world" → "hello-world"
    56→- "foo_bar" → "foo-bar"
    57→- "foo   bar" → "foo-bar"
    58→- "foo___bar" → "foo-bar"
    59→
    60→---
    61→
    62→### REQ-003: Character Filtering [MUST HAVE]
    63→
    64→**User Type**: Developer
    65→
    66→**Description**: The slugify function must remove all characters except letters, numbers, and hyphens.
    67→
    68→**Rationale**: Special characters and punctuation can cause encoding issues in URLs, break routing systems, or create security vulnerabilities. Restricting to alphanumeric and hyphen characters ensures maximum compatibility.
    69→
    70→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    71→- Letters (a-z) are preserved
    72→- Numbers (0-9) are preserved
    73→- Hyphens (-) are preserved
    74→- All other characters (punctuation, symbols, special characters) are removed
    75→- Character filtering applies after whitespace/underscore replacement
    76→
    77→**Examples**:
    78→- "hello, world!" → "hello-world"
    79→- "foo@bar.com" → "foobarcom"
    80→- "test#123" → "test123"
    81→
    82→---
    83→
    84→### REQ-004: Hyphen Normalization [MUST HAVE]
    85→
    86→**User Type**: Developer
    87→
    88→**Description**: The slugify function must collapse consecutive hyphens into a single hyphen.
    89→
    90→**Rationale**: Multiple consecutive hyphens reduce URL readability and may indicate processing errors. Normalizing to single hyphens ensures clean, professional-looking URLs.
    91→
    92→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    93→- Two or more consecutive hyphens are replaced with a single hyphen
    94→- Normalization happens after character filtering
    95→- Single hyphens are preserved unchanged
    96→
    97→**Examples**:
    98→- "a--b" → "a-b"
    99→- "a---b" → "a-b"
   100→- "a----b" → "a-b"
   101→
   102→---
   103→
   104→### REQ-005: Hyphen Trimming [MUST HAVE]
   105→
   106→**User Type**: Developer
   107→
   108→**Description**: The slugify function must remove leading and trailing hyphens from the result.
   109→
   110→**Rationale**: Leading or trailing hyphens appear unprofessional and may cause routing issues in some web frameworks. Clean trimming ensures slugs are ready for immediate use in URLs.
   111→
   112→**Acceptance Criteria**:
   113→- Any hyphens at the start of the string are removed
   114→- Any hyphens at the end of the string are removed
   115→- Trimming happens as the final step after all other transformations
   116→- Internal hyphens are not affected
   117→
   118→**Examples**:
   119→- "-hello-" → "hello"
   120→- "--foo--" → "foo"
   121→- "-a-b-" → "a-b"
   122→
   123→---
   124→
   125→### REQ-006: Empty String Handling [SHOULD HAVE]
   126→
   127→**User Type**: Developer
   128→
   129→**Description**: The slugify function should handle edge cases where input contains only special characters or whitespace.
   130→
   131→**Rationale**: Defensive programming prevents runtime errors and provides predictable behavior for all inputs.
   132→
   133→**Acceptance Criteria**:

   135→- Input consisting only of whitespace produces an empty string
   136→- Empty string input produces empty string output
   137→
   138→**Examples**:

   142→

   149→**As a** developer building a content management system

/**
 * Add two numbers.
 */
export function add(a: number, b: number): number {
  return a + b;
}

/**
 * Convert a string to a URL-friendly slug.
 *
 * Transforms input text by:
 * - Converting to lowercase
 * - Replacing spaces and underscores with hyphens
 * - Removing all characters except letters, numbers, and hyphens
 * - Collapsing consecutive hyphens into a single hyphen
 * - Trimming leading and trailing hyphens
 *
 * @param text - The input string to slugify
 * @returns A URL-friendly slug string
 *
 * @example
 * slugify("Hello, World!") // returns "hello-world"
 * slugify("foo_bar") // returns "foo-bar"
 * slugify("Test@Example.com") // returns "testexamplecom"
 */
export function slugify(text: string): string {
  return text
    .toLowerCase()
    .replace(/[\s_]+/g, '-')
    .replace(/[^a-z0-9-]/g, '')
    .replace(/-+/g, '-')
    .replace(/^-+|-+$/g, '');
}

     9→# Feature Requirements: Slugify String Utility
    10→
    11→## Overview
    12→
    13→This feature provides a string utility function that converts arbitrary text into URL-friendly slugs by normalizing whitespace, removing special characters, and applying consistent formatting rules.
    14→
    15→## Business Context
    16→
    17→URL slugs are a fundamental requirement for web applications, content management systems, and APIs. A reliable slugify utility ensures consistent, predictable URL generation across the application, improving SEO, user experience, and system interoperability.
    18→
    19→## Requirements
    20→
    21→### REQ-001: Text Normalization [MUST HAVE]
    22→
    23→**User Type**: Developer
    24→
    25→**Description**: The slugify function must convert input text to lowercase.
    26→
    27→**Rationale**: Lowercase normalization ensures URL consistency and prevents duplicate content issues where "Hello-World" and "hello-world" would be treated as different resources.
    28→
    29→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    30→- All uppercase letters (A-Z) are converted to lowercase (a-z)
    31→- Mixed-case input produces consistent lowercase output
    32→- Non-ASCII uppercase characters are handled according to locale-independent rules
    33→
    34→**Examples**:
    35→- "HELLO" → "hello"
    36→- "MixedCase" → "mixedcase"
    37→
    38→---
    39→
    40→### REQ-002: Whitespace and Underscore Replacement [MUST HAVE]
    41→
    42→**User Type**: Developer
    43→
    44→**Description**: The slugify function must replace spaces and underscores with single hyphens.
    45→
    46→**Rationale**: Hyphens are the web standard for word separation in URLs (as opposed to underscores or spaces), improving readability and SEO compatibility.
    47→
    48→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    49→- All space characters (U+0020) are replaced with a single hyphen (-)
    50→- All underscore characters (_) are replaced with a single hyphen (-)
    51→- Multiple consecutive spaces/underscores are collapsed into a single hyphen
    52→- Replacement happens before character filtering
    53→
    54→**Examples**:
    55→- "hello world" → "hello-world"
    56→- "foo_bar" → "foo-bar"
    57→- "foo   bar" → "foo-bar"
    58→- "foo___bar" → "foo-bar"
    59→
    60→---
    61→
    62→### REQ-003: Character Filtering [MUST HAVE]
    63→
    64→**User Type**: Developer
    65→
    66→**Description**: The slugify function must remove all characters except letters, numbers, and hyphens.
    67→
    68→**Rationale**: Special characters and punctuation can cause encoding issues in URLs, break routing systems, or create security vulnerabilities. Restricting to alphanumeric and hyphen characters ensures maximum compatibility.
    69→
    70→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    71→- Letters (a-z) are preserved
    72→- Numbers (0-9) are preserved
    73→- Hyphens (-) are preserved
    74→- All other characters (punctuation, symbols, special characters) are removed
    75→- Character filtering applies after whitespace/underscore replacement
    76→
    77→**Examples**:
    78→- "hello, world!" → "hello-world"
    79→- "foo@bar.com" → "foobarcom"
    80→- "test#123" → "test123"
    81→
    82→---
    83→
    84→### REQ-004: Hyphen Normalization [MUST HAVE]
    85→
    86→**User Type**: Developer
    87→
    88→**Description**: The slugify function must collapse consecutive hyphens into a single hyphen.
    89→
    90→**Rationale**: Multiple consecutive hyphens reduce URL readability and may indicate processing errors. Normalizing to single hyphens ensures clean, professional-looking URLs.
    91→
    92→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    93→- Two or more consecutive hyphens are replaced with a single hyphen
    94→- Normalization happens after character filtering
    95→- Single hyphens are preserved unchanged
    96→
    97→**Examples**:
    98→- "a--b" → "a-b"
    99→- "a---b" → "a-b"
   100→- "a----b" → "a-b"
   101→
   102→---
   103→
   104→### REQ-005: Hyphen Trimming [MUST HAVE]
   105→
   106→**User Type**: Developer
   107→
   108→**Description**: The slugify function must remove leading and trailing hyphens from the result.
   109→
   110→**Rationale**: Leading or trailing hyphens appear unprofessional and may cause routing issues in some web frameworks. Clean trimming ensures slugs are ready for immediate use in URLs.
   111→
   112→**Acceptance Criteria**:
   113→- Any hyphens at the start of the string are removed
   114→- Any hyphens at the end of the string are removed
   115→- Trimming happens as the final step after all other transformations
   116→- Internal hyphens are not affected
   117→
   118→**Examples**:
   119→- "-hello-" → "hello"
   120→- "--foo--" → "foo"
   121→- "-a-b-" → "a-b"
   122→
   123→---
   124→
   125→### REQ-006: Empty String Handling [SHOULD HAVE]
   126→
   127→**User Type**: Developer
   128→
   129→**Description**: The slugify function should handle edge cases where input contains only special characters or whitespace.
   130→
   131→**Rationale**: Defensive programming prevents runtime errors and provides predictable behavior for all inputs.
   132→

   135→- Input consisting only of whitespace produces an empty string
   136→- Empty string input produces empty string output

   145→## User Stories
   146→
   147→### STORY-001: URL Slug Generation
   148→
   149→**As a** developer building a content management system
   150→**I want** to convert article titles into URL-friendly slugs
   151→**So that** I can generate clean, readable URLs for content pages

   168→
   169→---

   171→### STORY-002: Consistent URL Normalization
   172→
   173→**As a** developer maintaining a web application

   175→**So that** I avoid duplicate routes and maintain URL integrity
   176→
   177→**Acceptance Criteria**:
   178→

   180→GIVEN inputs "Foo Bar", "foo_bar", and "FOO__BAR"
   181→WHEN I call slugify on each

   183→
   184→GIVEN an input with multiple consecutive hyphens "a---b"
   185→WHEN I call slugify(input)
   186→THEN I receive "a-b" with normalized hyphens
   187→```

   192→
   193→- Function handles all specified transformation rules correctly
   194→- Edge cases (empty strings, special characters only) are handled gracefully
   195→- Output matches expected format for all provided examples
   196→- Function is testable and documented for developer use

| AC-002-2 | All underscore characters (_) are replaced with a single hyphen (-) | VERIFIED | Test: `slugify("foo_bar")` returns `"foo-bar"` |
| AC-002-3 | Multiple consecutive spaces/underscores are collapsed into a single hyphen | VERIFIED | Regex `[\s_]+` matches one or more. Tests: `"foo   bar"` -> `"foo-bar"`, `"foo___bar"` -> `"foo-bar"` |
| AC-002-4 | Replacement happens before character filtering | VERIFIED | Pipeline order in code: replace spaces/underscores (line 40) precedes character filter (line 41) |

**Code Evidence**:

.replace(/[\s_]+/g, '-')
```

**Test Evidence**:

# Feature Requirements: Slugify String Utility

## Overview

This feature provides a string utility function that converts arbitrary text into URL-friendly slugs by normalizing whitespace, removing special characters, and applying consistent formatting rules.

## Business Context

URL slugs are a fundamental requirement for web applications, content management systems, and APIs. A reliable slugify utility ensures consistent, predictable URL generation across the application, improving SEO, user experience, and system interoperability.

## Requirements

### REQ-001: Text Normalization [MUST HAVE]

**User Type**: Developer

**Description**: The slugify function must convert input text to lowercase.

**Rationale**: Lowercase normalization ensures URL consistency and prevents duplicate content issues where "Hello-World" and "hello-world" would be treated as different resources.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- All uppercase letters (A-Z) are converted to lowercase (a-z)
- Mixed-case input produces consistent lowercase output
- Non-ASCII uppercase characters are handled according to locale-independent rules

**Examples**:
- "HELLO" → "hello"
- "MixedCase" → "mixedcase"

---

### REQ-002: Whitespace and Underscore Replacement [MUST HAVE]

**User Type**: Developer

**Description**: The slugify function must replace spaces and underscores with single hyphens.

**Rationale**: Hyphens are the web standard for word separation in URLs (as opposed to underscores or spaces), improving readability and SEO compatibility.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- All space characters (U+0020) are replaced with a single hyphen (-)
- All underscore characters (_) are replaced with a single hyphen (-)
- Multiple consecutive spaces/underscores are collapsed into a single hyphen
- Replacement happens before character filtering

**Examples**:
- "hello world" → "hello-world"
- "foo_bar" → "foo-bar"
- "foo   bar" → "foo-bar"
- "foo___bar" → "foo-bar"

---

### REQ-003: Character Filtering [MUST HAVE]

**User Type**: Developer

**Description**: The slugify function must remove all characters except letters, numbers, and hyphens.

**Rationale**: Special characters and punctuation can cause encoding issues in URLs, break routing systems, or create security vulnerabilities. Restricting to alphanumeric and hyphen characters ensures maximum compatibility.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Letters (a-z) are preserved
- Numbers (0-9) are preserved
- Hyphens (-) are preserved
- All other characters (punctuation, symbols, special characters) are removed
- Character filtering applies after whitespace/underscore replacement

**Examples**:
- "hello, world!" → "hello-world"
- "foo@bar.com" → "foobarcom"
- "test#123" → "test123"

---

### REQ-004: Hyphen Normalization [MUST HAVE]

**User Type**: Developer

**Description**: The slugify function must collapse consecutive hyphens into a single hyphen.

**Rationale**: Multiple consecutive hyphens reduce URL readability and may indicate processing errors. Normalizing to single hyphens ensures clean, professional-looking URLs.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Two or more consecutive hyphens are replaced with a single hyphen
- Normalization happens after character filtering
- Single hyphens are preserved unchanged

**Examples**:
- "a--b" → "a-b"
- "a---b" → "a-b"
- "a----b" → "a-b"

---

### REQ-005: Hyphen Trimming [MUST HAVE]

**User Type**: Developer

**Description**: The slugify function must remove leading and trailing hyphens from the result.

**Rationale**: Leading or trailing hyphens appear unprofessional and may cause routing issues in some web frameworks. Clean trimming ensures slugs are ready for immediate use in URLs.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Any hyphens at the start of the string are removed
- Any hyphens at the end of the string are removed
- Trimming happens as the final step after all other transformations
- Internal hyphens are not affected

**Examples**:
- "-hello-" → "hello"
- "--foo--" → "foo"
- "-a-b-" → "a-b"

---

### REQ-006: Empty String Handling [SHOULD HAVE]

**User Type**: Developer

**Description**: The slugify function should handle edge cases where input contains only special characters or whitespace.

**Rationale**: Defensive programming prevents runtime errors and provides predictable behavior for all inputs.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Input consisting only of special characters produces an empty string
- Input consisting only of whitespace produces an empty string
- Empty string input produces empty string output

**Examples**:
- "!!!" → ""
- "   " → ""
- "" → ""

---

## User Stories

### STORY-001: URL Slug Generation

**As a** developer building a content management system
**I want** to convert article titles into URL-friendly slugs
**So that** I can generate clean, readable URLs for content pages

**Acceptance Criteria**:

```gherkin
GIVEN an article title "Hello, World! A Beginner's Guide"
WHEN I call slugify(title)
THEN I receive "hello-world-a-beginners-guide"

GIVEN a product name "Super-Fast USB_3.0 Drive!!!"
WHEN I call slugify(name)
THEN I receive "super-fast-usb-30-drive"

GIVEN user input with leading/trailing whitespace " Foo Bar "
WHEN I call slugify(input)
THEN I receive "foo-bar"
```

---

### STORY-002: Consistent URL Normalization

**As a** developer maintaining a web application
**I want** slugify to produce consistent output for similar inputs
**So that** I avoid duplicate routes and maintain URL integrity

**Acceptance Criteria**:

```gherkin
GIVEN inputs "Foo Bar", "foo_bar", and "FOO__BAR"
WHEN I call slugify on each
THEN all produce the same output "foo-bar"

GIVEN an input with multiple consecutive hyphens "a---b"
WHEN I call slugify(input)
THEN I receive "a-b" with normalized hyphens
```

---

## Success Metrics

- Function handles all specified transformation rules correctly
- Edge cases (empty strings, special characters only) are handled gracefully
- Output matches expected format for all provided examples
- Function is testable and documented for developer use

---

## Out of Scope

The following are explicitly excluded from this feature:

- Unicode/non-ASCII character transliteration (e.g., "café" → "cafe")
- Custom separator configuration (always uses hyphen)
- Maximum length constraints or truncation
- Uniqueness guarantees or collision detection
- Database integration or persistence
- Localization or internationalization support

---

## Dependencies

- None identified. This is a pure string transformation utility.

---

## Assumptions

- Input is a string type (or can be coerced to string)
- English/ASCII character set is the primary use case
- Performance requirements are reasonable for typical string lengths (<10KB)
- Function will be used in a TypeScript/JavaScript environment based on project context

---

## Notes

This feature was gathered in AFK mode with the following decisions:

### AFK Decisions Log

| Decision Point | Choice | Rationale |
|----------------|--------|-----------|
| PRD Association | None (no PRDs found) | Work directory contains no PRD documents; feature is self-contained |
| Unicode Handling | Out of scope | Input specification focuses on ASCII; transliteration adds complexity beyond stated requirements |
| Empty String Behavior | Return empty string | Conservative default that prevents errors and matches intuitive expectations |
| Function Signature | slugify(text: string): string | Based on provided examples and TypeScript project context from KB |
| Error Handling | Defensive (return empty for invalid) | Prevents runtime exceptions; consistent with utility function patterns |

---

## Validation Examples

The following examples must all pass to satisfy requirements:

| Input | Expected Output | Requirements Validated |
|-------|----------------|----------------------|
| "Hello, World!" | "hello-world" | REQ-001, REQ-002, REQ-003, REQ-004, REQ-005 |
| " Foo__Bar " | "foo-bar" | REQ-002, REQ-005 |
| "a---b" | "a-b" | REQ-004 |
| "UPPERCASE" | "uppercase" | REQ-001 |
| "test@example.com" | "testexamplecom" | REQ-003 |
| "  " | "" | REQ-006 |
| "!!!" | "" | REQ-006 |
| "-leading-trailing-" | "leading-trailing" | REQ-005 |
| "foo___bar   baz" | "foo-bar-baz" | REQ-002, REQ-004 |

# Design: Slugify String Utility

**Feature ID**: slugify-string-utility
**Version**: 1.0.0
**Status**: Draft
**Created**: 2026-07-16

## Summary

The slugify utility is a pure TypeScript function added to the existing `src/utils.ts` module. It transforms arbitrary input text into URL-friendly slugs through a sequential pipeline of: lowercase normalization, whitespace/underscore replacement with hyphens, non-alphanumeric character removal, consecutive hyphen collapse, and leading/trailing hyphen trimming. This approach uses standard JavaScript string methods and regular expressions, requiring no external dependencies and matching the project's established pure-function pattern.

## Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph slugify["slugify(text: string): string"]
        A[Input Text] --> B[toLowerCase]
        B --> C[Replace spaces/underscores with -]
        C --> D[Remove non-alphanumeric except -]
        D --> E[Collapse consecutive -]
        E --> F[Trim leading/trailing -]
        F --> G[Output Slug]
    end
```

## Contracts

| Contract | Producer | Consumer | Required Fields Or Outputs |
|----------|----------|----------|----------------------------|
| slugify function | utils.ts | Application code | `slugify(text: string): string` - Returns normalized URL slug |

## Component Plan

| # | Component | Description | Files Changed |
|---|-----------|-------------|---------------|
| T1 | slugify function | Implement the slugify function with JSDoc documentation following existing utils.ts patterns | `src/utils.ts` |
| T2 | slugify tests | Add comprehensive test suite covering all requirements and edge cases | `src/utils.test.ts` |

## Implementation DAG

**Parallel Groups** (tasks with no inter-dependencies):

1. [T1] - Function implementation has no dependencies

**Dependencies**:

- T2 -> T1 (Interface: tests import slugify function from utils module)

**Critical Path**: T1 -> T2

## Validation Plan

| Behavior Or Contract | Failure Mode Covered | Test Type | Evidence Or Command |
|----------------------|----------------------|-----------|---------------------|
| REQ-001: Lowercase normalization | Uppercase chars not converted | unit | `bun test` - verify "HELLO" -> "hello" |
| REQ-002: Whitespace/underscore replacement | Spaces/underscores not replaced with hyphens | unit | `bun test` - verify "hello world" -> "hello-world", "foo_bar" -> "foo-bar" |
| REQ-002: Multiple consecutive whitespace collapse | Multiple spaces become multiple hyphens | unit | `bun test` - verify "foo   bar" -> "foo-bar" |
| REQ-003: Character filtering | Special chars not removed | unit | `bun test` - verify "hello, world!" -> "hello-world" |
| REQ-004: Hyphen normalization | Multiple hyphens not collapsed | unit | `bun test` - verify "a--b" -> "a-b" |
| REQ-005: Hyphen trimming | Leading/trailing hyphens remain | unit | `bun test` - verify "-hello-" -> "hello" |
| REQ-006: Empty string handling | Error thrown or incorrect output for edge cases | unit | `bun test` - verify "!!!" -> "", "   " -> "", "" -> "" |
| Combined transformation | Pipeline order incorrect | unit | `bun test` - verify "Hello, World!" -> "hello-world" |

## Documentation Impact

| Type | Target | Section | KB Source | Rationale |
|------|--------|---------|-----------|-----------|
| edit | .rp1/context/modules.md | Utils section | modules.md:Utils | Add slugify function to utils module documentation |

## Open Risks

| Risk | Impact | Mitigation |
|------|--------|------------|
| Unicode characters passed to function | LOW | Requirements explicitly scope to ASCII; non-ASCII chars simply removed per REQ-003 |

# Design Decisions: Slugify String Utility

**Feature ID**: slugify-string-utility
**Created**: 2026-07-16

## Decision Log

| ID | Decision | Choice | Rationale | Alternatives Considered |
|----|----------|--------|-----------|------------------------|
| D1 | Module location | Add to existing `src/utils.ts` | Follows established project pattern of utility functions in utils module; maintains single-file simplicity | Create new `src/slugify.ts` module - rejected to avoid unnecessary file proliferation for single function |
| D2 | Implementation approach | Sequential regex transformations | Clear, readable, maintainable; each step maps directly to a requirement; standard JS methods require no dependencies | Single complex regex - rejected for reduced readability; Character-by-character iteration - rejected as less performant and more verbose |
| D3 | Test location | Add to existing `src/utils.test.ts` | Follows project pattern of co-located tests in single test file | Separate test file - rejected to match existing test organization |
| D4 | Error handling | Return empty string for invalid input | Defensive programming prevents runtime errors; matches requirement REQ-006; consistent with utility function patterns | Throw error - rejected as overly strict for utility function; Return null - rejected as inconsistent return type |
| D5 | Transformation order | lowercase -> replace whitespace -> filter chars -> collapse hyphens -> trim | Each step builds on previous; replacement must happen before filtering so spaces become hyphens not removed; collapse after filter to catch hyphens created by char removal | Alternative orderings could cause bugs (e.g., trimming before collapse leaves edge hyphens) |

---

## AFK Mode: Auto-Selected Technology Decisions

| Decision | Choice | Source | Rationale |
|----------|--------|--------|-----------|
| Language | TypeScript | KB patterns.md | Project uses TypeScript exclusively |
| Test framework | Bun test runner | KB patterns.md | Project standard; `describe`/`test`/`expect` pattern |
| Module system | ESM exports | KB patterns.md | Project uses `"type": "module"` |
| Documentation | JSDoc comments | Codebase pattern | Existing utils.ts uses JSDoc for function documentation |
| Code style | TypeScript strict mode | KB patterns.md | Project enforces strict TypeScript |

    16→
    17→URL slugs are a fundamental requirement for web applications, content management systems, and APIs. A reliable slugify utility ensures consistent, predictable URL generation across the application, improving SEO, user experience, and system interoperability.

    23→**User Type**: Developer

    41→
    42→**User Type**: Developer
    43→
    44→**Description**: The slugify function must replace spaces and underscores with single hyphens.
    45→
    46→**Rationale**: Hyphens are the web standard for word separation in URLs (as opposed to underscores or spaces), improving readability and SEO compatibility.
    47→
    48→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    49→- All space characters (U+0020) are replaced with a single hyphen (-)

     9→# Feature Requirements: Slugify String Utility
    10→
    11→## Overview
    12→
    13→This feature provides a string utility function that converts arbitrary text into URL-friendly slugs by normalizing whitespace, removing special characters, and applying consistent formatting rules.
    14→
    15→## Business Context
    16→
    17→URL slugs are a fundamental requirement for web applications, content management systems, and APIs. A reliable slugify utility ensures consistent, predictable URL generation across the application, improving SEO, user experience, and system interoperability.
    18→
    19→## Requirements
    20→
    21→### REQ-001: Text Normalization [MUST HAVE]
    22→
    23→**User Type**: Developer
    24→
    25→**Description**: The slugify function must convert input text to lowercase.
    26→
    27→**Rationale**: Lowercase normalization ensures URL consistency and prevents duplicate content issues where "Hello-World" and "hello-world" would be treated as different resources.
    28→
    29→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    30→- All uppercase letters (A-Z) are converted to lowercase (a-z)
    31→- Mixed-case input produces consistent lowercase output
    32→- Non-ASCII uppercase characters are handled according to locale-independent rules
    33→
    34→**Examples**:
    35→- "HELLO" → "hello"
    36→- "MixedCase" → "mixedcase"
    37→
    38→---
    39→
    40→### REQ-002: Whitespace and Underscore Replacement [MUST HAVE]
    41→
    42→**User Type**: Developer
    43→
    44→**Description**: The slugify function must replace spaces and underscores with single hyphens.
    45→
    46→**Rationale**: Hyphens are the web standard for word separation in URLs (as opposed to underscores or spaces), improving readability and SEO compatibility.
    47→
    48→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    49→- All space characters (U+0020) are replaced with a single hyphen (-)
    50→- All underscore characters (_) are replaced with a single hyphen (-)
    51→- Multiple consecutive spaces/underscores are collapsed into a single hyphen
    52→- Replacement happens before character filtering
    53→
    54→**Examples**:
    55→- "hello world" → "hello-world"
    56→- "foo_bar" → "foo-bar"
    57→- "foo   bar" → "foo-bar"
    58→- "foo___bar" → "foo-bar"
    59→
    60→---
    61→
    62→### REQ-003: Character Filtering [MUST HAVE]
    63→
    64→**User Type**: Developer
    65→
    66→**Description**: The slugify function must remove all characters except letters, numbers, and hyphens.
    67→
    68→**Rationale**: Special characters and punctuation can cause encoding issues in URLs, break routing systems, or create security vulnerabilities. Restricting to alphanumeric and hyphen characters ensures maximum compatibility.
    69→
    70→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    71→- Letters (a-z) are preserved
    72→- Numbers (0-9) are preserved
    73→- Hyphens (-) are preserved
    74→- All other characters (punctuation, symbols, special characters) are removed
    75→- Character filtering applies after whitespace/underscore replacement
    76→
    77→**Examples**:
    78→- "hello, world!" → "hello-world"
    79→- "foo@bar.com" → "foobarcom"
    80→- "test#123" → "test123"
    81→
    82→---
    83→
    84→### REQ-004: Hyphen Normalization [MUST HAVE]
    85→
    86→**User Type**: Developer
    87→
    88→**Description**: The slugify function must collapse consecutive hyphens into a single hyphen.
    89→
    90→**Rationale**: Multiple consecutive hyphens reduce URL readability and may indicate processing errors. Normalizing to single hyphens ensures clean, professional-looking URLs.
    91→
    92→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    93→- Two or more consecutive hyphens are replaced with a single hyphen
    94→- Normalization happens after character filtering
    95→- Single hyphens are preserved unchanged
    96→
    97→**Examples**:
    98→- "a--b" → "a-b"
    99→- "a---b" → "a-b"
   100→- "a----b" → "a-b"
   101→
   102→---
   103→
   104→### REQ-005: Hyphen Trimming [MUST HAVE]
   105→
   106→**User Type**: Developer
   107→
   108→**Description**: The slugify function must remove leading and trailing hyphens from the result.
   109→
   110→**Rationale**: Leading or trailing hyphens appear unprofessional and may cause routing issues in some web frameworks. Clean trimming ensures slugs are ready for immediate use in URLs.
   111→
   112→**Acceptance Criteria**:
   113→- Any hyphens at the start of the string are removed
   114→- Any hyphens at the end of the string are removed
   115→- Trimming happens as the final step after all other transformations
   116→- Internal hyphens are not affected
   117→
   118→**Examples**:
   119→- "-hello-" → "hello"
   120→- "--foo--" → "foo"
   121→- "-a-b-" → "a-b"
   122→
   123→---
   124→
   125→### REQ-006: Empty String Handling [SHOULD HAVE]
   126→
   127→**User Type**: Developer
   128→
   129→**Description**: The slugify function should handle edge cases where input contains only special characters or whitespace.
   130→
   131→**Rationale**: Defensive programming prevents runtime errors and provides predictable behavior for all inputs.
   132→
   133→**Acceptance Criteria**:

   135→- Input consisting only of whitespace produces an empty string
   136→- Empty string input produces empty string output
   137→
   138→**Examples**:

   141→- "" → ""
   142→
   143→---
   144→
   145→## User Stories
   146→
   147→### STORY-001: URL Slug Generation
   148→
   149→**As a** developer building a content management system
   150→**I want** to convert article titles into URL-friendly slugs
   151→**So that** I can generate clean, readable URLs for content pages
   152→
   153→**Acceptance Criteria**:

   155→```gherkin
   156→GIVEN an article title "Hello, World! A Beginner's Guide"
   157→WHEN I call slugify(title)
   158→THEN I receive "hello-world-a-beginners-guide"
   159→
   160→GIVEN a product name "Super-Fast USB_3.0 Drive!!!"
   161→WHEN I call slugify(name)
   162→THEN I receive "super-fast-usb-30-drive"
   163→
   164→GIVEN user input with leading/trailing whitespace " Foo Bar "
   165→WHEN I call slugify(input)

/**
 * Add two numbers.
 */
export function add(a: number, b: number): number {
  return a + b;
}

/**
 * Convert a string to a URL-friendly slug.
 *
 * Transforms input text by:
 * - Converting to lowercase
 * - Replacing spaces and underscores with hyphens
 * - Removing all characters except letters, numbers, and hyphens
 * - Collapsing consecutive hyphens into a single hyphen
 * - Trimming leading and trailing hyphens
 *
 * @param text - The input string to slugify
 * @returns A URL-friendly slug string
 *
 * @example
 * slugify("Hello, World!") // returns "hello-world"
 * slugify("foo_bar") // returns "foo-bar"
 * slugify("Test@Example.com") // returns "testexamplecom"
 */
export function slugify(text: string): string {
  return text
    .toLowerCase()
    .replace(/[\s_]+/g, '-')
    .replace(/[^a-z0-9-]/g, '')
    .replace(/-+/g, '-')
    .replace(/^-+|-+$/g, '');
}

     9→# Feature Requirements: Slugify String Utility

    11→## Overview
    12→
    13→This feature provides a string utility function that converts arbitrary text into URL-friendly slugs by normalizing whitespace, removing special characters, and applying consistent formatting rules.
    14→
    15→## Business Context
    16→
    17→URL slugs are a fundamental requirement for web applications, content management systems, and APIs. A reliable slugify utility ensures consistent, predictable URL generation across the application, improving SEO, user experience, and system interoperability.
    18→
    19→## Requirements
    20→
    21→### REQ-001: Text Normalization [MUST HAVE]
    22→
    23→**User Type**: Developer
    24→
    25→**Description**: The slugify function must convert input text to lowercase.
    26→
    27→**Rationale**: Lowercase normalization ensures URL consistency and prevents duplicate content issues where "Hello-World" and "hello-world" would be treated as different resources.
    28→
    29→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    30→- All uppercase letters (A-Z) are converted to lowercase (a-z)
    31→- Mixed-case input produces consistent lowercase output
    32→- Non-ASCII uppercase characters are handled according to locale-independent rules
    33→
    34→**Examples**:
    35→- "HELLO" → "hello"
    36→- "MixedCase" → "mixedcase"
    37→
    38→---
    39→
    40→### REQ-002: Whitespace and Underscore Replacement [MUST HAVE]
    41→
    42→**User Type**: Developer
    43→
    44→**Description**: The slugify function must replace spaces and underscores with single hyphens.
    45→
    46→**Rationale**: Hyphens are the web standard for word separation in URLs (as opposed to underscores or spaces), improving readability and SEO compatibility.
    47→
    48→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    49→- All space characters (U+0020) are replaced with a single hyphen (-)
    50→- All underscore characters (_) are replaced with a single hyphen (-)
    51→- Multiple consecutive spaces/underscores are collapsed into a single hyphen
    52→- Replacement happens before character filtering
    53→
    54→**Examples**:
    55→- "hello world" → "hello-world"
    56→- "foo_bar" → "foo-bar"
    57→- "foo   bar" → "foo-bar"

    62→### REQ-003: Character Filtering [MUST HAVE]
    63→
    64→**User Type**: Developer

    66→**Description**: The slugify function must remove all characters except letters, numbers, and hyphens.
    67→
    68→**Rationale**: Special characters and punctuation can cause encoding issues in URLs, break routing systems, or create security vulnerabilities. Restricting to alphanumeric and hyphen characters ensures maximum compatibility.
